subject.title: CLI startup preflight can corrupt the live state DB while a gateway is running — health-check commands caused "database disk image is malformed" (2026.6.6, macOS); vanilla SQLite control does NOT reproduce

question: Should CLI health/status/stability avoid direct shared-state DB WAL maintenance while a gateway is running, and should OpenClaw enforce that through RPC-first read-only modes, a single-writer lease, or recovery-first quarantine?
rationale: The bug boundary is a persisted state/data-loss surface, but the durable fix changes CLI observability, doctor migrations, gateway ownership, and recovery behavior rather than one isolated function.

options.title: RPC-first, no-maintenance CLI
options.body: Make health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

options.title: Single-writer lease first
options.body: Have the gateway own write and WAL-maintenance access through an explicit lease, with other processes refusing writer-style shared DB opens while it is held.

options.title: Recovery-first quarantine
options.body: Add malformed openclaw.sqlite preservation/quarantine before prevention work, improving recovery while leaving the CLI/gateway maintenance race as follow-up.

recommendation.title: RPC-first, no-maintenance CLI
recommendation.body: Make health/status/stability prefer the running gateway and allow only read-only, no-checkpoint, no-migration file access while a gateway lease is active.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history and ownership signal for the shared DB contract is the shared SQLite introduction and repository ownership mapping.
